n.description: Input size: the largest n the solution must handle. Excludes patterns whose time complexity is infeasible at that n under the input-size guideline.

space.description: Space budget: the most extra memory allowed. Excludes patterns whose own space complexity is above it.

values.O(1): Extra memory at most constant, independent of n; in-place.
values.O(log n): Extra memory at most logarithmic in n.
values.O(sqrt(n)): Extra memory at most proportional to the square root of n.
values.O(n): Extra memory at most linear in n.
values.O(n log n): Extra memory at most n log n.
values.O(n * sqrt(n)): Extra memory at most n times the square root of n.
values.O(n^2): Extra memory at most quadratic in n.
values.O(n^2 log n): Extra memory at most n squared times log n.
values.O(n^3): Extra memory at most cubic in n.
values.O(2^n): Extra memory at most exponential in n.
values.O(n!): Extra memory at most factorial in n.
values.O(n^n): Extra memory at most n to the power n.

target_complexity.description: Time target: the slowest time complexity acceptable. Excludes patterns whose own time complexity is above it.

values.O(1): Time at most O(1): Constant time — mathematical formula or direct lookup; feasible at any n.
values.O(log n): Time at most O(log n): Binary search, balanced BST operations; handles enormous inputs; feasible up to n = 1,000,000,000,000.
values.O(sqrt(n)): Time at most O(sqrt(n)): Square root decomposition; trial division; feasible up to n = 1,000,000,000,000.
values.O(n): Time at most O(n): Single pass — linear scan, two pointers, sliding window, counting sort; feasible up to n = 100,000,000.
values.O(n log n): Time at most O(n log n): Sorting-based solutions; divide and conquer; feasible up to n = 10,000,000.
values.O(n * sqrt(n)): Time at most O(n * sqrt(n)): Mo's algorithm, some block decomposition; feasible up to n = 100,000.
values.O(n^2): Time at most O(n^2): Nested loops — brute force pairs, simple DP, 2D matrix traversal; feasible up to n = 10,000.
values.O(n^2 log n): Time at most O(n^2 log n): Sorting within quadratic loop; feasible up to n = 5,000.
values.O(n^3): Time at most O(n^3): Triple nested loops — Floyd-Warshall, interval DP, matrix multiplication; feasible up to n = 500.
values.O(2^n): Time at most O(2^n): Subset enumeration, bitmask DP; feasible up to n = 25.
values.O(n!): Time at most O(n!): Permutation generation, brute-force TSP; feasible up to n = 12.
values.O(n^n): Time at most O(n^n): Unrestricted backtracking; almost never acceptable; feasible up to n = 8.

updates.description: Problem trait: whether the data changes while it is being queried.

values.static: Built once and never modified while it is queried.
values.dynamic: Elements are inserted, deleted or modified between queries.

wildcard.description: Either: the data may or may not change between queries.

arrival.description: Problem trait: whether all input (and queries) is available up front or arrives over time and must be answered online.

values.batch: All input and queries are known before processing starts (offline).
values.streaming: Input or queries arrive one at a time and each must be handled as it arrives (online).

input_order.description: Problem trait: whether the input sequence is already sorted.

values.sorted: The input is already in sorted (or monotonic) order.
values.unsorted: The input has no useful order.

query_shape.description: Problem trait: what each query asks of the data.

values.point: Exact-key lookup or membership test; no ordering or range needed.
values.range_or_order: Range aggregates or order queries: range sums/min/max, floor/ceiling, predecessor/successor, rank, sorted iteration.
values.prefix: String-prefix queries such as prefix search or autocomplete.

exactness.description: Problem trait: whether every answer must be exactly correct or an approximate answer is acceptable.

values.exact: Every answer must be correct: no false positives, no near matches.
values.approximate: Approximate answers are acceptable: probabilistic false positives or near (fuzzy) matches.

value_sign.description: Problem trait: whether the numeric values (array elements or edge weights) can be negative.

values.non_negative: Every value is zero or positive.

graph_direction.description: Problem trait: whether the graph's edges are directed.

values.directed: Edges have a direction (u to v differs from v to u).

graph_weighting.description: Problem trait: whether the graph's edges carry weights or costs.

values.unweighted: Every edge counts the same (equal weight).
values.zero_one: Every edge weight is either 0 or 1.
values.weighted: Edges carry arbitrary weights or costs.
